headline: Gold prices drop by Tk6,590 per bhori in two days in Bangladesh
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has announced a new price reduction, bringing 22-carat gold down to Tk2,21,966 per bhori.
details: The price of gold jewelry in Bangladesh has decreased by a maximum of Tk3,324 per bhori in the latest update, according to the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS).
In a notification issued on Tuesday, BAJUS stated that the new prices became effective from 10:00 AM that day.
The price adjustment was decided by the BAJUS Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring after considering the overall market situation.
Currently, the price of 22-carat gold is set at Tk2,21,966 per bhori. 21-carat gold is now Tk2,11,993, and 18-carat gold is Tk1,82,075 per bhori.
Gold produced using traditional methods is now priced at Tk1,48,774 per bhori.
BAJUS noted that these prices will remain in effect across all jewelry stores until further notice, though making charges will apply based on the design of the jewelry.
The association also clarified that since VAT is already included in the sales price, jewelry stores cannot collect VAT separately from customers.
caption:

headline_marked: DMP bans [[public movement within 200 yards of HSC centres]]
headline: DMP bans public movement within 200 yards of HSC centres
summary: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police have issued a ban to ensure fair and peaceful examinations for over 1.2 million candidates.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) have prohibited the public from entering within 200 yards of Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examination centres in the city.
The ban, issued under the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Ordinance, aims to ensure that the exams are conducted in a fair and peaceful manner.
The order is in effect from July 2 until the conclusion of the exams. Only candidates and personnel related to the examinations are permitted entry.
Theory exams begin on July 2 with the Bangla First Paper and will continue until August 8, with practical exams concluding by August 15.
This year's HSC exams will feature common question papers for the nine general education boards, as well as the madrasah and technical education boards.

Candidates must enter their centres 30 minutes before the start of the exams. The first 30 minutes will consist of multiple-choice questions, followed by two and a half hours of essay-based questions.
